chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi', from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Aiman ibn Mohraz, who narrated it from Al-Qasim [and] ibn Faz'al, that Hariz said:
Whoever performs Hajj for three consecutive years, then performs Hajj or does not perform Hajj, he is in the status of one who is habitual in Hajj.
The compiler of this book said: May God increase his support: This chain of narration is weak/unstable, and I did not change it because it was thus in my manuscript, and the hadith is sound.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Hajj for three consecutive years in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration in *Al-Khisal* to highlight the spiritual discipline of consistency in Hajj, using the metaphor of an 'addict' to denote deep-rooted habituation rather than mere repetition. Although the chain of narration (*isnad*) is noted as *mudtarib* (unstable or fluctuating), the compiler preserves it as sound (*sahih*) based on his manuscript, reflecting the Shia scholarly practice of valuing the content's reliability even when the chain has minor irregularities. This emphasizes the virtue of making Hajj a sustained, habitual act of worship rather than a sporadic obligation.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-100 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Al-Sindy ibn al-Rabi’a, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Fuzayl ibn Yasar, on the authority of Aiman ibn Mohraz, who quoted on the authority of Al-Qasim and ibn Faz’zal that Harizat said, “Whoever goes on the Hajj pilgrimage for three consecutive years it is as if he has gone on the Hajj pilgrimage every year whether he continues to go on the Hajj or not in the following years.”

The compiler of the book - may God increase his honor - said, “The chain of narrations of this tradition is weak. However, I have cited it as it was in my manuscript. However, there is a correct form of this tradition on the authority of Imam as-Sadiq (MGB) that is cited next.”
